candidate_spec.high_level_variant: Ego slightly offset laterally within the lane and with a small forward speed bias near the same signalized junction, keeping overall displacement minimal so that the oracle still flags a red-light violation without explicit evidence of crossing the stop line or lane boundaries.
candidate_spec.mutation_intent: Tests whether a small change in ego pose and low-speed behavior near the junction preserves an oracle red violation in a scene with static environment, available traffic-light states, and no dynamic actors, while maintaining ambiguity about the precise physical infraction.
pre_execution_validation_rules: Interpret actor_index=0 as the ego vehicle when applying actor_mutations; do not introduce any non-ego dynamic actors.
Confirm that the ego remains within the same logical approach lane toward the junction; lateral offset must not clearly place the ego into an adjacent lane.
Verify that traffic-light state data is being published before the ego begins to move, and that the junction remains signal-controlled.
post_execution_validation_rules: Verify oracle red=true with crash=false, stuck=false, lane_invasion=false at run completion.
Ensure ego net displacement from start to end remains small (e.g., limited forward creep, not a full intersection traversal).

Check that no explicit stop-line crossing event or clear route–signal linkage is recorded in planner or map-matching logs; if such evidence exists, classify as deviating from the intended ambiguous mechanism.
Confirm that any dataset-style lane invasion indicators are not used as ground truth; rely only on the online oracle flags when comparing to the root-cause pattern.
uncertainty: Small lateral and speed adjustments may alter planner or perception behavior in ways that change how the oracle evaluates red violations; this variant intentionally explores that regime while still targeting the same high-level outcome.
The exact spatial relation between ego, lane markings, and stop line remains under-specified; validation must avoid assuming a particular geometry when judging red-light causality.
